newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea mulls delay of plan to free oil prices.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea mulls delay of plan to free oil prices.

text.p: South Korea may delay its plan to free domestic oil prices and reinstitute advance notice requirements on petrol price increases, a senior energy ministry official said on Tuesday.
"The advance notice system has produced a positive outcome by preventing volatility in pricing and consumer confusion," he told Reuters by telephone.
"We are thinking of keeping the system longer than planned. The final decision would be announced in the near future."

Domestic prices of petrol, kerosene, diesel and C-type fuel were deregulated on Jan 1 and were no longer subject to a government-set monthly price ceiling. In the first six months of deregulation, oil refiners were required to report price changes on petrol, kerosene and diesel to the government in advance.
But after six months, the government had said refiners would be allowed to report price changes after the fact.
